newsitem.title: USA: US LPG market falls following API monthly data.
newsitem.headline: US LPG market falls following API monthly data.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices fell in moderate activity on Friday following the release of industry data showing sharp stock builds, players said.
The monthly American Petroleum Institute data late Thursday showed total U.S. propane stocks up by 7.2 million barrels to 32.8 million as of April 30, putting stocks 43 percent above year-ago levels.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, propane parcels sold at 35.25 cents and 35.00 cents, about a quarter cent below Thursday.
The Midwest came off by a half cent, trading at 36.50 cents.
"It's all in reaction to the API data," said a Midwest trader.
The heavies were largely stable despite a 4.2 million build to 15.99 million barrels, which is four percent below year-ago levels.
Ethane, however, shed strength at midday on Friday. The API data reported stocks up by 2.1 million barrels to 18.9 million, or 26 percent above last year.
Belvieu ethane purity was heard done at 20.75 cents and 21.00 cents, a half cent below yesterday. Conway material was down a quarter at 18.00/18.25 cents.

Meanwhile, Pemex was heard looking for a butane cargo from an international source. On Thursday the state-owned oil and gas monopoly was rumored to have bought a 30,000-tonne Saudi Arabian cargo of propane and butane.
The monopoly said yesterday that it has restarted its Cactus plant to 95 percent of capacity. Output had been severely reduced by an explosion last July.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
